newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-CARBAJAL RETAINS TITLE, CHAVEZ WINS ON RETURN TO RING.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-CARBAJAL RETAINS TITLE, CHAVEZ WINS ON RETURN TO RING.

text.p: Michael Carbajal made a successful second defence of his International Boxing Federation junior flyweight title on Saturday when he knocked out Tomas Rivera in the fifth round.

Carbajal was never in trouble against Rivera as he improved to 43-2 with 27 knockouts and positioned himself for a possible showdown with unbeaten World Boxing Council strawweight champion Ricardo Lopez.
"When I'm focused like this I just believe no one can beat me," Carbajal said. "I was relaxed and throwing my combinations well, and throwing some tight punches."
Carbajal knocked Rivera to the canvas twice in the fourth round before using a left-right-left combination to again put him down with 1:26 left in the fifth round.
Rivera was unable to reach his feet by the count of 10 and fell to 13-2-2.
"I knew I was going to catch him with the right hand coming in," said Carbajal, who won the title with a second-round knockout of Melchor Cob Castro of Mexico.
"He came in and tried to take the title from me but unfortunately for him, it didn't happen."
Three-time former champion Julio Cesar Chavez returned to the ring for the first time since he was beaten to a bloody pulp by Oscar de la Hoya in four rounds on June 7.
The legendary Mexican champion stopped Joey Gamache when the American failed to answer the bell for the ninth round. of their non-title junior welterweight bout.
Chavez was in control throughout and pounded Gamache with a barrage of punches in the eighth round.
Bleeding excessively from around the eyes, Gamache gamely fought back but he had nothing left after the punishing eighth round as Chavez took his record to 98-2-1.
"I was 100 percent tonight, not like when I fought de la Hoya," said Chavez, who likely earned a rematch with de la Hoya with his convincing victory Saturday.
"I fought a hell of a fight, but he was just too good for me," said Gamache, who lost for the third time in 48 fights.
